metadata.technology_reasoning: Man-portable thermal imaging sights are handheld or weapon-mounted devices that utilize uncooled or cooled infrared detectors to provide thermal imaging for target acquisition and situational awareness. They are widely adopted by military and law enforcement due to their portability, discrete operation without visible light, and battery-powered electronic architecture.

components.reasoning: The core sensing element capturing the thermal infrared radiation, usually a microbolometer array or cooled photon detector, always present and separate as a distinct module.
Critical for focusing infrared radiation onto the detector, includes germanium or other IR-transmissive lenses; standard separate subassembly.
Processes raw detector data into usable thermal images, typically a dedicated PCB with DSP or FPGA processors, standard and procured separately.
Provides the user interface for viewing thermal images, usually an OLED or LCD microdisplay, a separate modular component.
Supplies portable electrical power; battery packs are standard separate components, often rechargeable lithium-ion.
Protective structural casing that integrates and protects internal components; manufactured and procured as a distinct assembly.
Buttons, switches, or joystick for operating settings; commonly a distinct subassembly or integrated with electronics board, common but sometimes integrated.

Infrared (IR) Detector Module.name: Germanium
Infrared (IR) Detector Module.reasoning: Germanium is a standard semiconductor material used in infrared detectors for its narrow bandgap and high IR sensitivity, universally essential for IR detector function.

Infrared (IR) Detector Module.name: Silicon

Infrared (IR) Detector Module.name: Copper
Infrared (IR) Detector Module.reasoning: Essential electrical conductor for internal wiring and connection in the detector module, universally used with very few substitutes.

Infrared (IR) Detector Module.name: Aluminum
Infrared (IR) Detector Module.reasoning: Used as metallization and heat sinks in IR modules, standard material rarely substituted for this role.
